test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2022: Official Paper (Held On: 13 March, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
**Some parts of a sentence have been jumbled up, and labelled P, Q, R and S. Select the option that gives the correct sequence in which these parts can be rearranged to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence.**

Many psychological, neurological 

P. and different thinking skills that make them leaders rather than followers

Q. studies generally indicate that leaders truly are born with different personality traits

R. to discover if leadership truly can be a learned trait, and

S. and sociological tests have been conducted by scientists
solution:
Here the correct answer is **SRQP**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct sequence to form a meaningful and grammatically correct sentence is: **SRQP**.
 
• The sentence can be arranged as follows:
 
 
• **Many psychological, neurological,** ​
 
• **S. **and sociological tests have been conducted by scientists
 
• **R.** to discover if leadership truly can be a learned trait, and
 
• **Q.** studies generally indicate that leaders truly are born with different personality traits
 
• **P.** and different thinking skills that make them leaders rather than followers
 
 
 
• This sequence forms a coherent sentence that discusses the research conducted to understand if leadership is an innate trait or can be learned.
 
• 
 
S: This part continuous the introduction of the idea that tests have been conducted by scientists. It sets the stage for the rest of the sentence and highlights the research conducted in the field.

 
 
• 
 
R: "to discover if leadership truly can be a learned trait, and"

 This part explains the purpose of the tests mentioned in part S. Scientists conducted these tests to explore whether leadership can be acquired or learned, implying the potential influence of nurture in developing leadership skills.

 
 
• 
 
Q: "studies generally indicate that leaders truly are born with different personality traits"

 This segment introduces the findings from studies. It suggests that research generally supports the notion that leaders have inherent or inborn qualities, specifically different personality traits.

 
 
• 
 
P: "and different thinking skills that make them leaders rather than followers."

 The final part of the rearranged sequence elaborates on the traits mentioned in Q. It highlights that leaders possess distinct thinking skills that set them apart from followers, implying a combination of innate abilities and acquired knowledge.
